ptsP.description: PtsP is the GAF-domain-containing enzyme I(Ntr) that initiates the nitrogen-regulatory phosphotransferase relay in Pseudomonas putida KT2440. It accepts phosphate from phosphoenolpyruvate and transfers it to the NPr phosphocarrier, thereby coupling metabolic state to the phosphorylation state of the terminal regulator PtsN.

review.summary: PtsP is the soluble entry enzyme of the PTS(Ntr) phosphorelay.
review.reason: The UniProt localization and lack of transmembrane segments support a cytoplasmic enzyme.

review.summary: PtsP transfers phosphate from PEP into the PTS(Ntr) protein relay.
review.reason: In vivo KT2440 analysis establishes PEP as the phosphate source and PtsP as enzyme I(Ntr).

review.summary: PtsP participates in a regulatory phosphorelay, not sugar transport or phosphorylation.
review.reason: PMID:18296519 explicitly describes the PtsP-PtsO-PtsN branch as unrelated to sugar traffic.

review.summary: PtsP transfers a phosphorus-containing group between metabolites and proteins.
review.reason: Correct broad parent of the more informative GO:0008965 activity.

review.summary: PtsP initiates a protein phosphorelay by accepting phosphate from PEP and phosphorylating NPr.
review.reason: The KT2440 phosphorylation-state study directly establishes PtsP as the entry enzyme in the PEP-to-NPr-to-PtsN protein-phosphorylation sequence.

supported_by.supporting_text: Our results show that the source of phosphate available to the system is PEP and that the primary flow of phosphate through the N/C-sensing PTS proceeds from PEP to EI(Ntr) to NPr to EIIA(Ntr).

ptsH.description: PtsH/PP_0948 is the NPr phosphocarrier of the nitrogen-regulatory phosphotransferase system in Pseudomonas putida KT2440, historically called ptsO in the experimental literature. It relays phosphate from PtsP enzyme I(Ntr) to the terminal EIIA(Ntr) regulator PtsN. Under fructose-growth conditions, FruB provides an alternative phosphate input into the NPr/PtsN branch.

ptsN.description: PtsN is the terminal EIIA(Ntr) component of the nitrogen-regulatory phosphotransferase system in Pseudomonas putida KT2440. It receives phosphate from NPr/PtsO and acts as a phosphorylation-state-dependent regulatory adaptor. It directly controls KdpD-dependent potassium-transport regulation and, in its non-phosphorylated form, binds and inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase E1/AceE; it is not a sugar-transport enzyme.

review.summary: PtsN is an EIIA-like regulatory phosphoprotein but does not transfer phosphate to carbohydrate.
review.reason: PMID:18296519 shows that this PTS(Ntr) branch is unrelated to sugar traffic.

review.summary: PtsN belongs to a regulatory phosphorelay, not a sugar uptake PTS.
review.reason: The experimentally characterized KT2440 branch lacks a permease and does not phosphorylate sugar.

review.summary: PtsN directly regulates KdpD, but the direction of the regulatory output is lineage dependent.
review.reason: Dephosphorylated E. coli IIA(Ntr) activates KdpD, whereas KT2440 PtsN, mainly in its phosphorylated state, represses kdpFABC transcription through direct KdpD interaction. Protein kinase regulator activity captures the conserved mechanism without incorrectly fixing the direction as activation.

supported_by.supporting_text: Two-hybrid data and biochemical analysis revealed that IIA(Ntr) interacts with sensor kinase KdpD and stimulates kinase activity, resulting in increased levels of phosphorylated response regulator KdpE.
Measurements of kdpFp promoter activity in different pts mutants showed that PtsN is responsible for repression of kdpFABC transcription.

review.summary: PtsN is the terminal phospho-state signal readout of the intracellular PTS(Ntr) relay.
review.reason: The KT2440 study establishes ordered phosphate flow to PtsN, whose phosphorylation state controls downstream regulatory interactions.

supported_by.supporting_text: Our results show that the source of phosphate available to the system is PEP and that the primary flow of phosphate through the N/C-sensing PTS proceeds from PEP to EI(Ntr) to NPr to EIIA(Ntr).

supported_by.supporting_text: Bacterial two-hybrid assays demonstrated that kdpFp regulation is implemented through direct interaction of the PtsN protein with the sensor kinase KdpD of the KdpD/KdpE two-component system.

review.reason: Target-organism interaction and activity assays establish direct, non-covalent inhibition of PDH by the non-phosphorylated PtsN species.

supported_by.supporting_text: Both genetic and biochemical evidence revealed that the non-phosphorylated form of PtsN is the protein species that inhibits PDH.
